title: Following Length Constraints in Instructions

model.params_source: assumed (the paper gives no decoding parameters for the AlpacaEval-LI runs; Appendix E states temperature 0.7 only for MT-Bench-LI, where sampling was used to expand the set). max_tokens 1024 is ours: the largest target length in the released file is 764 words.

task.subset_rule: all 802 AlpacaEval-LI prompts (805 AlpacaEval 2 instructions minus the 3 that already carry an explicit length constraint, Sec. 3.2)
task.approximation: decoding parameters are assumed (see params_source); the paper's own generations are not published, so only the aggregate Vlt% can be compared.

items.source: AlpacaEval-LI release of the paper (facebookresearch/RAM, projects/length_instruct README): length_instructed_alpaca_baseline.json
items.license: MIT (facebookresearch/RAM LICENSE); the underlying AlpacaEval 2 prompts are CC BY-NC 4.0 (tatsu-lab/alpaca_eval)

fields_prose.input: instruction = the length-instructed prompt (Figure 1 template already applied: 'Answer the following instruction using <MAX_LEN> words or less.\n\n<ORIGINAL_INSTRUCTION>')
fields_prose.label: max_len = target word limit for that prompt (minimum generation length of GPT-4 Turbo 11/06, Claude 3 Opus 02/29 and Mistral Large 24/02 on the original prompt, Sec. 3.1.1)
fields_prose.id: none in the file; the runner numbers the rows

download.check: GET, 1,358,975 bytes, application/json; 802 rows, every row has an integer max_len (range 1-764) and an instruction starting with 'Answer the following instruction using '

prompt.source_location: Figure 1 (length-instruction template) + Sec. 3.2; the released AlpacaEval-LI file stores the already-augmented prompt
prompt.verbatim: full (the template of Figure 1 is 'Answer the following instruction using <MAX_LEN> words or less.\n\n<ORIGINAL_INSTRUCTION>'; the released items.instruction field is exactly that string with the two slots filled, so the prompt is taken from the release rather than re-assembled)

output.postprocess: none (the whole reply is the response whose words are counted)
output.parse_paper: none: the full generation is scored

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Vlt% = percentage of the 802 responses whose word count exceeds that prompt's max_len; the word count is Appendix A's function (nltk.word_tokenize, tokens that are pure punctuation dropped). Implemented in harness/tierb/hooks/W4400065264.py.
metric.original_location: Table 2, row 'GPT4 Turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)', AlpacaEval-LI Vlt(%) column

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run 2026-09-19: prepare's own figure is $10.14 (400 output tokens assumed per call), the battery dry run reports $25.15 because it bills the full max_tokens=1024; real spend will sit between the two (802 items, 0 unrenderable).

notes: Only the Vlt% cell is re-executed. The Win% column of the same table needs the AlpacaEval 2 pairwise judge against the released baseline answers (field `output` of the same file) and is a separate, judge-dependent run. nltk's punkt/punkt_tab data must be present for the hook's word count (nltk.download('punkt_tab')); it was installed on 2026-09-19 on this machine. Seeds 1 because the paper's cost tier is high; the item bootstrap gives the CI.
